spec_evidence.checked: Cached vercel OAS snapshots: in v1.27.0 the type:snowflake connector branch carries key-pair auth material (serviceUsername, serviceRole, privateKeyPem, publicKeyPem, publicKeyFingerprint). In v1.28.0 the type:snowflake branch is reduced to clientName + accountIdentifier (+ optional defaultSessionRole/extras) and a new type:snowflake-wif branch appears; privateKeyPem survives only in an unrelated schema (paired with clientSecret/slug). The removed properties have no in-schema successor within the connector create payload.

fix.migration_guide: The Snowflake connector auth model changed: key-pair credential fields (serviceUsername, serviceRole, publicKeyPem, publicKeyFingerprint) were removed from the connector create payload, and a separate snowflake-wif (workload identity federation) connector type was introduced. Deleting the removed properties from the request restores schema validity but leaves the connector without usable auth material — migrating requires provisioning new credentials (WIF setup or the new snowflake auth flow) on both the Vercel and Snowflake sides. That is credential/infrastructure provisioning a codemod cannot generate, matching the twilio MessageFlow and shopify mTLS precedents: the breaking element is a business-supplied input, not a code shape.
fix.example_before: await client.post('/v1/connect/connectors', { data: { clientName, accountIdentifier, serviceUsername, serviceRole, publicKeyPem, publicKeyFingerprint } });
